## P01 — 3-Year Consolidated P&L Model Specification (Simulated)  
**Purpose (per SOP-2026-Q3-Rev5):** Define the structure, scope, periodization, consolidation rules, and required line items for a **simulated 3-year consolidated P&L** that explicitly includes **gross margin compression points**, **unexpected SG&A logistics spikes**, and **reported vs adjusted EBITDA with reconciliations**, ready for **APEX SOSE Command Center intake gate**.

---

# 1) Scope & Time Granularity

## 1.1 Horizon
- **3 full fiscal years** (FY1, FY2, FY3), simulated.
- Start/end dates must be explicit (e.g., **FY1 = 2024-01 to 2024-12**), configurable.

## 1.2 Period granularity (explicit)
Choose one; default is **monthly** for intake readiness:
- **Monthly** periods: 36 columns (YYYY-MM), plus quarterly and annual rollups as optional derived views.
- If **quarterly** is used instead: 12 columns (FYx-Qy).  
**Requirement:** Periods must be contiguous with no gaps; each period must have:
- Period start date
- Period end date
- Fiscal year and fiscal period index

## 1.3 Currency & units
- Single presentation currency (e.g., USD) with explicit header field: `PresentationCurrency`.
- Values in **full units** (not thousands) unless `ScaleFactor` is set and documented.

---

# 2) Consolidation Structure & Rules

## 2.1 Consolidated view requirement
Model must output:
- **Consolidated Total** P&L (single view required for intake), AND optionally:
- Entity-level tabs and a consolidation bridge.

## 2.2 Multi-entity roll-up (recommended spec)
Entities:
- `OpCo_A`, `OpCo_B`, `OpCo_C` (configurable)
- `HoldCo` (optional)

Consolidation method:
- Line-by-line summation across entities into **Consolidated**.
- Intercompany treatment:
  - Intercompany revenue/COGS captured in dedicated lines and **eliminated** in consolidation.

## 2.3 Elimination guidance (minimum required)
Provide explicit elimination lines in the consolidated layer:
- `Intercompany Revenue (Elimination)` (negative revenue)
- `Intercompany COGS (Elimination)` (positive COGS)
- Optional: `Intercompany Management Fees (Elimination)` in SG&A/Other OpEx as applicable

**Rule:** Consolidated totals must reflect **net-of-eliminations** values.

---

# 3) Required P&L Line Items (Minimum Intake Set)

## 3.1 Core operating lines (must exist)
1. **Revenue**
2. **COGS**
3. **Gross Profit** (= Revenue − COGS)
4. **Gross Margin %** (= Gross Profit / Revenue)

## 3.2 Operating expense lines (must exist)
5. **SG&A (Total)**  
   - Must include a separate sub-line:
   - **SG&A — Logistics** (explicitly modeled)
   - Recommended additional SG&A sub-lines for realism (optional but structured):
     - SG&A — Sales & Marketing
     - SG&A — G&A / Corporate
     - SG&A — Customer Support
6. **Other OpEx (Total)** (non-SG&A operating costs; can include R&D, facility ops, etc.)

## 3.3 Earnings lines (must exist)
7. **EBITDA (Reported)**  
   - Defined as: Gross Profit − SG&A (Total) − Other OpEx (Total)  
   - (No D&A, interest, taxes in this model unless separate below-the-line section is added as optional.)
8. **EBITDA Adjustments (Total)** (sum of adjustment categories; see §6)
9. **EBITDA (Adjusted)** (= EBITDA (Reported) + EBITDA Adjustments (Total))

**Sign convention requirement:**  
- Expenses positive in their natural sign OR negative—must be consistent; specify in metadata.  
- Recommended: Revenue positive; expenses positive; profit lines calculated (Revenue − expenses).

---

# 4) Gross Margin Compression Points — Requirements

## 4.1 Definition
A “compression point” is a period where **Gross Margin % declines materially versus baseline** with an attributed driver.

## 4.2 Timing & frequency (minimum)
Model must include, across the 36 months:
- **At least 3 distinct compression events** (non-overlapping start months), distributed across the horizon (e.g., one per year minimum).
- Each event must specify:
  - `StartPeriod` and `EndPeriod`
  - `Magnitude_bps` (basis point decline in GM% vs baseline)
  - `AttributionDriverCode` (see below)
  - `Notes` (plain-language explanation)

## 4.3 Magnitude specification
Each compression event must include:
- GM% reduction expressed as:
  - **basis points** (e.g., −150 bps), and/or
  - direct COGS uplift delta (e.g., +$X)
- Must reconcile mathematically in the period P&L (i.e., GM% drop must be caused by COGS increase and/or Revenue mix/price changes).

## 4.4 Attribution driver codes (required enumeration)
At least one driver code per event:
- `INPUT_COST_INFLATION` (materials, fuel, packaging)
- `FREIGHT_SURCHARGE_COGS` (inbound freight classified in COGS)
- `PROMO_DISCOUNTING` (price/discount pressure)
- `MIX_SHIFT_LOW_MARGIN` (product/customer/channel mix)
- `YIELD_SCRAP` (manufacturing yield loss, scrap)
- `SUPPLIER_MOQ` (MOQ / unfavorable purchase economics)
- `FX_IMPACT` (if multi-currency entities exist; otherwise omit)

## 4.5 Baseline definition (must be documented)
Baseline GM% must be defined in metadata as one of:
- Rolling trailing 3-month average pre-event
- FY-to-date pre-event average
- Fixed plan GM% assumption

---

# 5) SG&A — Logistics Spike Requirements

## 5.1 Definition
A “logistics spike” is an **unexpected, time-bounded increase** in `SG&A — Logistics` beyond modeled run-rate.

## 5.2 Frequency & duration (minimum)
Across the 36 months:
- **At least 2 spike events** (recommended 3–5).
- Each event must specify:
  - `SpikeStartPeriod`, `SpikeEndPeriod`
  - `SpikeAmount` (absolute $ increase) and/or `SpikePct` vs baseline
  - `DurationPeriods` (integer months or quarters)
  - `ReasonCode` (required; see below)
  - `IsOneTime` flag (true/false)
  - `ReversalPattern` (e.g., immediate drop-off, taper, partial persistence)

## 5.3 Reason codes (required enumeration)
- `CARRIER_RATE_SHOCK`
- `EXPEDITED_SHIPPING`
- `WAREHOUSE_OVERFLOW`
- `3PL_TRANSITION`
- `ROUTING_ERROR_REWORK`
- `LABOR_OVERTIME_DISTRIBUTION`
- `CLAIMS_REDELIVERY`
- `SYSTEM_OUTAGE_MANUAL_PROCESSING`

## 5.4 Baseline logistics run-rate
Must document how baseline logistics is set:
- fixed monthly run-rate, or
- % of revenue with min/max guardrails.

---

# 6) EBITDA Adjustments — Categories & Reconciliation Rules

## 6.1 Adjustment framework (must exist)
Provide **reported vs adjusted** view with category-level adjustments. Required categories:
1. **One-time / Non-recurring**
   - e.g., restructuring, severance, facility closure, litigation settlement
2. **Non-cash**
   - e.g., stock-based compensation (if treated as adjustment), unrealized gains/losses
3. **Run-rate normalization**
   - e.g., remove temporary inefficiencies, add back start-up costs until steady state
4. **Transaction / Integration**
   - e.g., diligence, deal fees, integration consulting

Optional categories (allowed if documented):
- `COVID_OR_FORCE_MAJEURE`
- `InsuranceRecoveries` (note sign rules)
- `AssetDisposalGainsLosses` (if above-the-line in EBITDA)

## 6.2 Reconciliation rule (must be enforced)
For each period:
- `EBITDA (Adjusted) = EBITDA (Reported) + Σ(Adjustment Categories)`
- Provide a reconciliation block with:
  - category line items
  - subtotal = EBITDA Adjustments (Total)

## 6.3 Governance fields per adjustment line (required)
Each adjustment category row must carry:
- `AdjustmentID`
- `Category`
- `Description`
- `StartPeriod`, `EndPeriod`
- `Amount`
- `SupportabilityFlag` (e.g., High/Med/Low for simulation; intake may require)
- `AuditNote`

---

# 7) Model Layout (Spreadsheet/Tables) — Structural Spec

## 7.1 Required tabs (or equivalent tables)
1. `README_Intake` (metadata + instructions)
2. `Assumptions_Log` (structured)
3. `Entity_Input` (entity-period line items; long-form table preferred)
4. `Consolidation_Elims` (intercompany and other eliminations)
5. `Consolidated_PnL` (final intake view)
6. `EBITDA_Adjustments` (detail + reconciliation)
7. `Events_GM_Compression` (event registry)
8. `Events_Logistics_Spikes` (event registry)
9. `Audit_Notes` (change log / known limitations)

## 7.2 Data shape requirement
APEX intake-friendly “tidy” format (preferred):
- Columns: `ScenarioID, Version, Entity, Period, LineItem, Amount, Currency, Notes`
Plus computed consolidated pivot/view for humans.

---

# 8) Intake-Gate Metadata Requirements (Must Be Present)

## 8.1 Required header metadata fields
- `ScenarioID` (unique; e.g., SIM-FY24FY26-BASE-001)
- `ScenarioName`
- `Version` (semantic or incremental; e.g., v0.3)
- `ModelOwner` (role/person placeholder acceptable for simulation)
- `CreatedDate`
- `LastUpdatedDate`
- `TimeGranularity` (Monthly/Quarterly)
- `FiscalCalendarDefinition` (month-end rule)
- `PresentationCurrency`
- `ScaleFactor`
- `ConsolidationScope` (single entity vs multi-entity)
- `EntitiesIncluded`
- `EliminationPolicySummary`
- `SignConvention`
- `EBITDA_Definition` (explicit text)
- `BaselineDefinitions` (GM baseline, logistics baseline)

## 8.2 Assumptions log (minimum fields)
- `AssumptionID`
- `Driver` (e.g., pricing, volume, COGS inflation)
- `Value`
- `EffectivePeriodStart/End`
- `Rationale`
- `SourceOrSimulationMethod`
- `SensitivityNotes`

## 8.3 Audit notes / controls
- `ChangeLog` entries: what changed, when, why
- `KnownLimitations`
- `ReconciliationChecksPassed` (Y/N) for:
  - GP = Rev − COGS
  - EBITDA roll-forward
  - Consolidation ties to entity sums net elims

---

# 9) Validation & Acceptance Checks (for intake readiness)

Minimum automated checks (can be formulas):
- No missing periods (36/12 as selected)
- No divide-by-zero in GM%
- Consolidated = Σ entities + eliminations (line-by-line)
- EBITDA adjusted reconciliation matches exactly each period
- Event registries tie to financial deltas:
  - GM compression event periods show GM% drop >= specified threshold
  - Logistics spike periods show SG&A logistics uplift >= specified threshold

---

## Evidence, Assumptions, Unresolved Gaps (per SOP-2026-Q3-Rev5)

### Evidence used
- **User request** specifies: 3-year consolidated P&L spreadsheet, includes **gross margin compression points**, **unexpected SG&A spikes in logistics**, and **EBITDA adjustments** for **APEX SOSE Command Center intake gate**.
- **Acceptance criteria** provided in the prompt dictates required lines, consolidation guidance, event requirements, and metadata.

### Assumptions made (to complete spec)
- Monthly granularity is the default for intake readiness; quarterly allowed as an alternative.
- Multi-entity consolidation is included with elimination lines to satisfy “roll-up with elimination guidance.”
- EBITDA is treated as operating EBITDA (pre D&A/interest/tax) unless the user later specifies otherwise.

### Unresolved gaps (need confirmation outside P01, not executed here)
- Exact entity list (single vs specific OpCos), fiscal year start month, and currency.
- Whether D&A is required below EBITDA for this intake gate (not requested, so excluded from minimum).
- Any Command Center-specific file naming conventions or template constraints not included in the prompt.

### P05 — Model Unexpected SG&A Spikes in Logistics (Anomaly Events)  
Grounded to SOP-2026-Q3-Rev5 intake expectations: anomalies must be separately classifiable, time-bound, reason-coded, and reconcilable to EBITDA via a bridge.

---

## 1) SG&A Logistics sub-line structure (simulation-ready)
**Create/confirm these rows in the SG&A section (annual or monthly/quarterly periods):**
- **SG&A – Logistics (Baseline Run-Rate)** *(expected/recurring)*
- **SG&A – Logistics (Unexpected Spikes)** *(anomaly-only; must be zero unless event)*
- **SG&A – Logistics (Total)** = Baseline + Unexpected  
- **SG&A (Total)** rolls up including Logistics (Total)

**Flagging fields (columns or adjacent table)**
- `Is_Unexpected` (TRUE/FALSE) — must be TRUE for spikes
- `Reason_Code` (enumerated)
- `Event_ID`
- `Start_Period`, `End_Period`
- `Magnitude` (total $ and/or $/period)

---

## 2) Baseline run-rate (kept stable to preserve model integrity)
**Assumption (editable):** baseline logistics SG&A run-rate is constant within each year unless your broader model already has seasonality.  
Example baseline (annual view; can be distributed evenly by month/quarter):
- **FY1:** $1.20m  
- **FY2:** $1.26m *(+5% inflation)*  
- **FY3:** $1.32m *(+5% inflation)*  

This baseline is **not** tagged unexpected and is not part of anomaly bridge.

---

## 3) Unexpected spike events (minimum 2; separately trackable)
Below are **three** simulated events to exceed the minimum requirement. Use your model period grain (Month/Quarter/Year). If annual-only P&L, allocate to the year totals and document intra-year timing in the event log.

### Event Log (to place in a dedicated “Logistics Spike Register” tab)
| Event_ID | Unexpected? | Reason_Code | Period Range | Magnitude | Allocation Method | Explanation |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---|---|
| LXS-001 | TRUE | Carrier_Surcharge | FY1 Q3–Q4 | **+$0.38m** | Even across impacted periods | Major carriers imposed peak season + fuel surcharge step-up mid-year; not budgeted. |
| LXS-002 | TRUE | Expedited_Freight | FY2 Q2 | **+$0.22m** | 100% in Q2 | Customer OTIF recovery after supplier delay required air/expedite. |
| LXS-003 | TRUE | Warehousing_Overflow | FY3 Q1–Q2 | **+$0.30m** | 60% Q1 / 40% Q2 | Temporary overflow warehouse and handling labor due to DC capacity constraint. |

**Reason code set (example controlled vocabulary):**
- `Carrier_Surcharge`, `Expedited_Freight`, `Warehousing_Overflow`, `Disruption`  
(Keep these consistent across the dataset for SOSE ingestion.)

---

## 4) How to model the spikes in the P&L (mechanics)
### A) Period-level entry (recommended)
In the **SG&A – Logistics (Unexpected Spikes)** row, enter values only in impacted periods:
- FY1 Q3: +$0.19m, FY1 Q4: +$0.19m (for LXS-001)
- FY2 Q2: +$0.22m (for LXS-002)
- FY3 Q1: +$0.18m, FY3 Q2: +$0.12m (for LXS-003)

All other periods: **0**.

### B) Roll-up formulas
- `Logistics_Total[t] = Logistics_Baseline[t] + Logistics_Unexpected[t]`
- `SGA_Total[t] = SUM(SGA sub-lines including Logistics_Total[t])`
- `EBITDA[t] = Gross_Profit[t] - SGA_Total[t] - Other_Opex[t]`  
(Or your model’s EBITDA definition; the key is the spike impacts flow through exactly once.)

---

## 5) Bridge / reconciliation (separately trackable)
Create a small EBITDA bridge section with a dedicated line:
- **EBITDA impact – Logistics unexpected spikes** = `-1 * SUM(Logistics_Unexpected[t])` per period/year

This must reconcile:  
`EBITDA_with_spikes - EBITDA_without_spikes = - Logistics_Unexpected`

Where:
- `EBITDA_without_spikes` uses the same model but sets `Logistics_Unexpected[t]=0`.

---

## 6) QA checks (must pass for acceptance)
### QA-1: Logistics roll-up integrity
For every period `t`:  
- **Check:** `Logistics_Total[t] - (Baseline[t] + Unexpected[t]) = 0`

### QA-2: SG&A roll-up integrity
For every period `t`:  
- **Check:** `SGA_Total[t] - SUM(all SG&A sub-lines) = 0`  
(including Logistics_Total)

### QA-3: Unexpected spikes are properly flagged and non-overlapping
- **Check:** all spike event rows have `Is_Unexpected=TRUE`
- **Check:** any period’s Unexpected value can be traced to ≥1 Event_ID (no “orphan” dollars)

### QA-4: EBITDA reconciliation
For every period `t`:  
- **Check:** `(EBITDA_with_spikes[t] - EBITDA_without_spikes[t]) + Logistics_Unexpected[t] = 0`

---

## Evidence, assumptions, unresolved gaps
**Evidence (from request / acceptance):**
- Logistics must be a **distinct SG&A sub-line** with baseline + additive spikes.
- Need **≥2 spike events** with **period ranges, magnitudes, and reason codes**.
- Spikes must be **flagged unexpected** and **separately trackable** in a bridge.
- QA must confirm SG&A roll-up and EBITDA reconciliation to spike impacts.

**Assumptions (explicit, editable):**
- Baseline logistics SG&A grows ~5% YoY (can be replaced with your model’s baseline).
- Period grain can be quarterly; if monthly, distribute as specified by allocation method.
- Spikes hit SG&A (not COGS); classification is “Logistics SG&A” per objective.

**Unresolved gaps (need inputs to finalize to your exact spreadsheet):**
- Your model’s period grain (Monthly vs Quarterly vs Annual).
- Currency and scaling ($, $000, $m).
- Whether any logistics items belong in COGS (freight-in) vs SG&A (freight-out); I kept all anomalies in **SG&A logistics** per primitive scope.
- Exact EBITDA definition used in your consolidated P&L (e.g., treatment of stock comp/one-offs).

If you provide period grain + scaling, I can restate the exact per-column entries (cells) for the spike row and the bridge lines without changing anything outside P05.

primitives.title: Implement EBITDA Adjustments & Reconciliation (Reported vs Adjusted)
primitives.objective: Add an EBITDA adjustment layer that produces both reported EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA with a clear bridge and auditability for intake.
acceptance: Model outputs both Reported EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA for every period and for annual totals.
Adjustment categories are listed with positive/negative sign conventions and mapped to periods (e.g., one-time restructuring, non-cash charges, settlements).
A bridge table reconciles Reported EBITDA to Adjusted EBITDA and ties out to P&L line impacts where applicable.
Adjustments are uniquely identified, documented, and do not break core accounting identities or rollups.
QA checks validate that Adjusted EBITDA = Reported EBITDA + Net Adjustments for all periods.
